tagline.text: A white-sand beach just a short walk down from the southern Cebu highway

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangays Daan-Lungsod and Guiwang, Alcoy, Cebu, along Natalio Bacalso Avenue

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800~2,000 (per day, by public transport from Cebu City)

children.text: Tingko Beach is a white-sand beach right beside the highway in Alcoy, on Cebu's southeastern coast. It is about 92km from Cebu City, reachable by a single bus ride, and makes an easy stop on the way to Oslob.

Tingko Beach sits in the town of Alcoy on the southeastern coast of Cebu Island. According to Wikipedia, the beach spans two barangays, Daan-Lungsod and Guiwang, right beside Natalio Bacalso Avenue, the town's main road. Alcoy is about 92km from Cebu City, and as you drive the southern highway toward Oslob or Santander you will see beach signs along the roadside.

The appeal of this beach is its easy access and simplicity. A short walk down from the highway brings you to a stretch of white sand, and the water is clear and shallow enough that it is not stressful to bring children. Nipa-roofed cottages line the sand, with a few private resorts tucked in between. There are no big facilities or flashy activities, but it is a good place for a day trip from Cebu City or a rest stop during a southern Cebu journey.

The sea in front of the beach is known as a low reef flat. Sea grass and rocks lie close to shore, so walking barefoot is uncomfortable at low tide. It suits swimming and light snorkeling, and it is best not to expect deep-water activities. Alcoy also has the Nug-as forest, called Cebu's last rainforest, so you can combine the sea and the mountains in one itinerary.

Tingko Beach appears to be run in several separate sections. Many accounts say the public stretch charges only a small environmental fee, while named private sections such as Antig Tingko Beach Resort charge their own entrance fee. Fees and rules differ by section, so it is safest to check at the entrance before going in. Alcoy is a small town of about 19,000 people (2024 census). According to Wikipedia, old watchtowers once used to watch for pirates still stand in Daan-Lungsod and Guiwang, and they are counted among the town's oldest surviving structures. Taking a quick look at the town while you rest at the beach makes the trip richer. Every year on
August 23

, the Siloy Festival in honor of St. Rose of Lima raises awareness of the Black Shama bird and eco-tourism. The town gets crowded during the festival and transport and rooms fill up quickly, so keep that in mind when planning.

blocks.title: A beach right off the highway

children.text: Get off the bus, cross the road, and a short walk brings you to the sand. You do not need to hire a motorbike or tricycle, which suits a light day trip. Traffic on the highway is fast, though, so take care when crossing.
The sand is white, the water is clear, and the depth is low, so it is good for swimming and playing in the water. Some stretches near shore have sea grass and rocks, so water shoes are recommended.

blocks.title: A day of rest in a nipa cottage

children.text: Roofed cottages line the sand, which makes it easy to escape the midday sun. The daily rate is reported at about

depending on size, so ask for the price before you negotiate. Cottages have shade and a table, which is handy for laying out a packed lunch, and on peak-season weekends they tend to fill up early in the morning.
You can look underwater with a mask and snorkel over the shallow reef and sea grass. Visibility varies a lot with sea conditions, so go in on a calm morning.

blocks.title: A rest stop on the southern drive

children.text: It lies roughly midway along the coastal road from Cebu City to Oslob, so it combines well with Oslob, Boljoon, and Dalaguete. It works better as a stop to break the journey than as a place to stay for long.

blocks.title: Nug-as forest and the Black Shama

children.text: The Nug-as forest in the hills of Alcoy is known as a place to see the Black Shama, locally called siloy. Visits are usually arranged through the Alcoy Tourism Office with a guide and an early start.

items.title: Cebu City day trip
items.subtitle: A beach day by round-trip bus

children.text: Take a bus bound for Oslob, Santander, or Bato via Oslob at the Cebu South Bus Terminal. Tell the conductor in advance that you want to get off at Tingko Beach.
Get off in front of Tingko Beach, cross the road, and walk down to the beach. Pay the fee at the entrance and find a cottage or shaded spot.
Swim and snorkel in the shallow sea. At low tide, wear water shoes and watch the bottom as you walk.
Eat the packed lunch you brought, or get snacks and grilled food from the beach stalls. There are not many restaurants.
Relax on the beach or stroll along the sand. There is little shade at midday, so use a cottage or a hat.
Go back up to the highway and flag down a northbound bus to Cebu City. Check the last bus time in advance.
The bus takes about 3–4 hours one way, so you do not get a long stay at the beach. Staying overnight or pairing it with Oslob is more relaxed than doing it all in one day.
Leave Cebu City and stop for snacks in Dalaguete or Argao along the way.
Enjoy swimming and a cottage rest at Tingko Beach in Alcoy.
Travel by bus or rental car past Boljoon to Oslob and check in to your lodging.
Visit Oslob's Tumalog Falls or Sumilon Island, then return to Cebu City.
With a rental car or a car with driver, you can stay at Tingko Beach for just an hour or two and move on to the next stop.
A direct flight from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
From Mactan-Cebu Airport, take a taxi or a ride-hailing car to the Cebu South Bus Terminal. The time varies with traffic.
At the Cebu South Bus Terminal, take a bus bound for Oslob, Santander, or Bato via Oslob. Do not take a Bato via Barili bus, because it goes to the west coast.
The trip takes about
3–4 hours
depending on traffic. Tell the conductor you want to get off at Tingko Beach and he will let you know.
Fares differ between sources and a recent increase has been reported, so check at the ticket booth. To return, flag down a northbound bus toward Cebu City from the roadside.
Buses run along the coastal highway all day, but they may thin out in the evening, so check the last bus time.
From Cebu City, drive about
92km
along Natalio Bacalso Avenue (the southern coastal highway).
Parking fees differ by private section, and some sources mention about ₱100, so check at the entrance.
Within Alcoy, tricycles and habal-habal (motorbike taxis) cover short distances. Agree on the fare before you ride.
On the steep road toward Nug-as in the hills, people often travel by habal-habal.
Southern Cebu has a tropical climate, and the average temperature in Alcoy is about
. Wikipedia gives annual rainfall of about 1,396mm, but these figures are from weather models, so treat them as a guide.
Visitor reports say the sea is calmest and clearest in March–May. December–February is also pleasant, but weekends and holidays are crowded with families, so a weekday visit is much quieter.

If you want to see the sunrise, one guide describes dawn views from Mt. Campetra in the hills of Alcoy. Combining that with a beach day means staying overnight, so first consider whether you can start early.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Good for swimming and walks, but busy on weekends in peak season
Calmest, clearest sea, good for snorkeling. Shade is a must at midday
Waves and visibility can worsen, and avoid visiting during typhoon season

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary with local conditions.
There are a few private resorts and simple rooms around Tingko Beach. A 2022 blog about Antig Tingko Beach Resort listed room rates of about
, but it is safest to check current rates and contact details directly before booking. There are more choices farther south in Oslob. Book ahead for peak-season weekends.

Restaurants are few. Beach stalls sell drinks, snacks, and grilled food, but for a proper meal you need to go to the Alcoy town market area or as far as Oslob. That is why many families bring packed lunches and water. It is best to take your trash home.

The southern coast can be reached by public transport, but buses are sometimes spaced far apart, so if you plan to stay overnight, check both your check-in time and the last bus. Rules on outside food or pool use may differ by private section, so just ask at the entrance.
Bring plenty of small cash. Many places take fees, cottages, and snacks in cash only.
Some shallow stretches have sea grass and rocks, so bring water shoes.
There is little natural shade at midday, so bring a hat and sunscreen or rent a cottage.
Weekends and holidays are crowded, so arriving on a weekday morning is easier.
There is a notice that tents are no longer allowed, so do not plan to camp.
When crossing the highway, look both ways carefully because cars travel fast.
Find out the return bus time in advance and head up to the roadside before sunset.
For the Nug-as forest and Black Shama visits, inquire through the Alcoy Tourism Office ((032) 326-2217).
When getting off the bus, tell the conductor whether you want to stop at the Tingko or Antig entrance.
Fees and rules differ by section and fee information varies between sources. Check the fee and what it includes at the entrance first.
This is a shallow sea with coral, rocks, and sea grass, so do not step on or touch the coral.
At low tide the bottom is exposed and walking barefoot is risky. Wear shoes.
Avoid swimming on days with strong waves and currents or when a typhoon is approaching.
Do not leave valuables in the cottage while you are away.
Fees and rules in this guide are as far as could be confirmed in 2026 and may change. Check the latest notices.
Oslob
, continuing to the south, is known for whale shark tourism and Tumalog Falls, and is about
30–45 minutes
from Tingko Beach by bus.
Tumalog Falls
inland from Oslob pairs well with the beach for a full-day itinerary.
Sumilon Island
, a sandbar island reached by boat from Oslob, is easy to add to a southern itinerary.
Osmeña Peak
, to the north toward Dalaguete, is the highest point in Cebu and is known for early-morning sunrise treks.
The Nug-as forest in the hills of Alcoy is called Cebu's last rainforest and is known for Black Shama watching. Inquire at the Alcoy Tourism Office for visits.
